title: Familiar verbs with singular partitive
summary: Use a singular partitive object with these waiting, helping and listening verbs: Odotan bussia. — I am waiting for a bus.
objectives: Choose a singular partitive object with familiar waiting, helping and listening constructions.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Choose a singular partitive object with familiar waiting, helping and listening constructions.
A verb can govern a case: its usual construction asks for a particular word form. Learn the whole pattern rather than translating an English preposition into a separate Finnish word.
The selected objects refer to one person or thing. Their complete forms and the conjugated verbs are provided.
keyPoints: In the ordinary waiting, helping and listening meanings taught here, use a partitive object.

examples.english: I am waiting for a bus.
steps: In the ordinary waiting, helping and listening meanings taught here, use a partitive object.
Odotan means “I am waiting for” and works as the verb. odotan comes from odottaa: odota- + -n, with tt → t.
bussia means “bus” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep bussi and add -a: bussi + a = bussia.

examples.english: I am waiting for a train.
steps: In the ordinary waiting, helping and listening meanings taught here, use a partitive object.
Odotan means “I am waiting for” and works as the verb. odotan comes from odottaa: odota- + -n, with tt → t.
junaa means “train” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep juna and add -a: juna + a = junaa.
In the ordinary waiting, helping and listening meanings taught here, use a partitive object.
Autan means “I help” and works as the verb. autan comes from auttaa: auta- + -n, with tt → t.
ystävää means “friend” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep ystävä and add -ä: ystävä + ä = ystävää.

examples.english: I am listening to a teacher.
steps: In the ordinary waiting, helping and listening meanings taught here, use a partitive object.
Kuuntelen means “I am listening to” and works as the verb. kuuntelen comes from kuunnella: kuuntele- + -n, with nn → nt and the e stem.
opettajaa means “teacher” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep opettaja and add -a: opettaja + a = opettajaa.

commonMistakes: English for or to need not become a separate word in these Finnish patterns.
Use the object form even when the person or thing is specific.
